e7_s3: Gastric involvement in systemic lupus erythematosus
e7_s4_rationale: The patient has Sjögren’s syndrome and the histologic findings show foveolar hyperplasia and mild degeneration of parietal cells, which is consistent with gastric involvement in Sjögren’s syndrome. The negative anti-parietal cell antibody and normal vitamin B12 levels also support this diagnosis.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Autoimmune gastritis
e7_s4_rejected.why: Negative anti-parietal cell antibody and normal vitamin B12 levels do not support this diagnosis

e7_s4_rejected.label: Chronic atrophic gastritis
e7_s4_rejected.why: The biopsy findings do not show significant atrophy or metaplasia, which is typical of chronic atrophic gastritis

e7_s4_rejected.label: Gastric involvement in systemic lupus erythematosus
e7_s4_rejected.why: There is limited evidence to suggest that systemic lupus erythematosus directly involves the stomach in this manner

e7_s4_rejected.label: Atrophic corpus gastritis
e7_s4_rejected.why: The biopsy findings do not show significant atrophy of the gastric corpus, which is typical of atrophic corpus gastritis
